title: Classification of Three-dimensional Electron Diffraction Data with a Large Language Model
problem: Three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) generates hundreds to thousands of molecular structures per sample, but many are inaccurate due to noise and measurement limitations. Manual inspection is time-consuming and labor-intensive.
motivation: 3D ED enables high-resolution structure determination for tiny crystals unsuitable for X-ray diffraction, but quality control bottlenecks limit throughput. Automated screening can dramatically reduce manual inspection workload.
method: LLM-centric automatic screening method: (1) converts atomic coordinates to topology-only language representation, (2) applies rule-based filtering, (3) fine-tunes LLM on correct vs. artificially-corrupted molecules, (4) groups identical topologies.
key_novelty: Novel application of fine-tuned LLMs to scientific structure classification, using topology-only language representation tailored to 3D ED data.
contributions: Reduced manual inspection burden by 95.8% on average
Evaluation on seven real 3D ED datasets
Efficient large-scale classification of scientific data
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. LLM model details not specified. Training data generation procedure for corrupted molecules not detailed.
primary_theme: LLM-based automated screening for scientific data analysis
